status_4xx.name: Client error (4xx)
status_4xx.desc: The URL returns a 4xx status code; users and search engines cannot reach the content.
status_4xx.fix: If the page moved, 301-redirect it to the new address; if it was removed, update or remove internal links pointing to it.

status_5xx.name: Server error (5xx)
status_5xx.desc: The server failed to fulfil the request. Persistent 5xx errors can hurt crawling and indexing.
status_5xx.fix: Check server/application logs, fix the cause and confirm the page returns 200.

fetch_error.name: Connection error
fetch_error.desc: The page could not be fetched (timeout, DNS, SSL or network error).
fetch_error.fix: Make sure the domain resolves, the SSL certificate is valid and the server responds in time; increase the timeout if needed.

blocked_security.name: Not crawled for security reasons
blocked_security.desc: The target resolves to a local/private or otherwise blocked address; SSRF protection blocked the request.
blocked_security.fix: For public sites, check DNS records. For local development sites enable localhost mode in .env and in the crawl settings.

redirect_temporary.name: Temporary redirect (302/303/307)
redirect_temporary.desc: The URL uses a temporary redirect. For a permanent move, temporary redirects can blur signals.
redirect_temporary.fix: Use 301 or 308 if the move is permanent.

meta_refresh_redirect.name: Meta refresh redirect
meta_refresh_redirect.desc: The page redirects with <meta http-equiv="refresh">. Server-side redirects are more reliable.
meta_refresh_redirect.fix: Replace the meta refresh with a server-side 301 redirect.

internal_link_http.name: HTTP internal link on HTTPS page
internal_link_http.desc: An HTTPS page links to HTTP URLs on the same site, causing unnecessary redirects and mixed signals.
internal_link_http.fix: Update internal links to point directly to HTTPS URLs.

mixed_content_image.name: Mixed content (HTTP image)
mixed_content_image.desc: An HTTPS page loads images over HTTP; browsers may block them or show warnings.

slow_response.name: Slow server response
slow_response.desc: Downloading the page took longer than the threshold. This is a single measurement taken during the crawl, not real-user (field) data.
slow_response.fix: Improve server response time (caching, database queries, hosting) and measure again.

body_truncated.name: Response body truncated
body_truncated.desc: The page exceeded the configured maximum size, so only part of it was analysed.
body_truncated.fix: Reduce the page size or raise ZERQON_MAX_BODY_BYTES in .env.

redirect_chain.name: Redirect chain
redirect_chain.desc: The URL redirects in more than one step. Each hop adds latency and wastes crawl budget.
redirect_chain.fix: Redirect the start URL to the final target in a single hop and update internal links to the final URL.

redirect_loop.name: Redirect loop
redirect_loop.desc: The redirects loop back on themselves; the page can never be reached.
redirect_loop.fix: Fix the redirect rules so the chain ends on a page returning 200.

redirect_to_error.name: Redirect to an error page
redirect_to_error.desc: The redirect chain ends on a page returning 4xx/5xx.
redirect_to_error.fix: Redirect to a working, relevant page or fix the target page.

internal_link_to_redirect.name: Internal link to a redirect
internal_link_to_redirect.desc: The page links to internal URLs that redirect.
internal_link_to_redirect.fix: Point internal links directly at the final (200) URL.

broken_internal_link.name: Broken internal link
broken_internal_link.desc: The page links to internal URLs that return 4xx/5xx or cannot be reached.
broken_internal_link.fix: Update links to working pages or remove them; add suitable 301 redirects for removed content.

http_https_duplicate.name: HTTP and HTTPS both accessible
http_https_duplicate.desc: Both the HTTP and HTTPS versions of the same page return 200, creating duplicate content.
http_https_duplicate.fix: 301-redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS and set the canonical to the HTTPS version.

url_too_long.name: Long URL
url_too_long.desc: The URL exceeds the configured length threshold. This is not a strict search engine rule; it concerns readability and shareability.
url_too_long.fix: Prefer shorter, descriptive URLs; add a 301 redirect when changing them.

url_parameters.name: URL with parameters
url_parameters.desc: The URL contains query parameters, which can create duplicate URL variations.
url_parameters.fix: Use canonicals on parameter variations and remove unnecessary parameters from internal links.

url_uppercase.name: Uppercase in URL
url_uppercase.desc: The URL path contains uppercase letters. Paths are case-sensitive on many servers, which can create duplicates.
url_uppercase.fix: Use lowercase URLs and 301-redirect uppercase variations.

url_underscores.name: Underscores in URL
url_underscores.desc: The URL path contains underscores. Hyphens are generally recommended as word separators.
url_underscores.fix: Separate words with hyphens in new URLs; use 301s if existing URLs must change.

url_double_slash.name: Double slash in URL
url_double_slash.desc: The URL path contains consecutive slashes, usually caused by faulty link generation, which can create duplicates.
url_double_slash.fix: Fix the template/code generating the link and redirect variations to a single URL.

url_variant_duplicates.name: Duplicate URL variations
url_variant_duplicates.desc: Several URLs differing only by case, trailing slash, www, index file or parameter order return 200 for the same page.
url_variant_duplicates.fix: Choose one preferred URL; 301-redirect the others or point them to it with a canonical.

title_missing.name: Missing title
title_missing.desc: The page has no <title> tag. The title is a key signal that may be used as the headline in search results.
title_missing.fix: Add a unique title that describes the page content.

title_empty.name: Empty title
title_empty.desc: The <title> tag exists but is empty.
title_empty.fix: Write a descriptive text in the title tag.

title_multiple.name: Multiple titles
title_multiple.desc: The page has more than one <title> tag, making it unclear which one is used.

title_too_short.name: Short title
title_too_short.desc: The title is below the configured minimum length and may not describe the page well enough.
title_too_short.fix: Expand the title to include the topic and distinguishing information.

title_too_long.name: Long title
title_too_long.desc: The title exceeds the configured maximum and may be truncated in search results. The threshold is not a strict rule.
title_too_long.fix: Shorten the title, putting the most important information first.

title_h1_mismatch.name: Title and H1 mismatch
title_h1_mismatch.desc: The title and the first H1 share no meaningful words. Not always a problem, but can be an inconsistent signal.
title_h1_mismatch.fix: Make sure the title and H1 describe the same topic.

title_duplicate.name: Duplicate title
title_duplicate.desc: The same title is used on several indexable pages; the pages may be hard to tell apart.
title_duplicate.fix: Give each page its own title, or use a canonical if the content really is the same.

description_missing.name: Missing meta description
description_missing.desc: The page has no meta description. Search engines may generate a snippet from the page content.
description_missing.fix: Add a unique meta description summarising the page.

description_empty.name: Empty meta description
description_empty.desc: The meta description tag exists but is empty.
description_empty.fix: Write a summary in the tag or remove it.

description_multiple.name: Multiple meta descriptions
description_multiple.desc: The page has more than one description tag.

description_too_short.name: Short meta description
description_too_short.desc: The description is below the configured minimum length.
description_too_short.fix: Expand the description to convey the page's value.

description_too_long.name: Long meta description
description_too_long.desc: The description exceeds the configured maximum and may be truncated in search results.
description_too_long.fix: Shorten it, putting the key information first.

description_duplicate.name: Duplicate meta description
description_duplicate.desc: The same description is used on several indexable pages.
description_duplicate.fix: Write an original description for each page.

h1_missing.name: Missing H1
h1_missing.desc: The page has no H1 heading. The H1 communicates the main topic to users and search engines.
h1_missing.fix: Add an H1 describing the main topic of the page.

h1_multiple.name: Multiple H1s
h1_multiple.desc: The page has more than one H1. Valid in HTML5, but it can blur the main topic.
h1_multiple.fix: Use one main H1 and move other headings into the H2-H6 hierarchy.

heading_empty.name: Empty heading
heading_empty.desc: There are H1-H6 tags without content.
heading_empty.fix: Remove empty headings or add meaningful text.

heading_skip_level.name: Skipped heading level
heading_skip_level.desc: The heading hierarchy skips a level (e.g. H1 to H3), an illogical transition for accessibility and content structure.
heading_skip_level.fix: Use headings in sequential levels (H1 → H2 → H3).

h1_duplicate.name: Duplicate H1
h1_duplicate.desc: The same H1 is used on several indexable pages.
h1_duplicate.fix: Tailor each page's H1 to its own content.
